signals.entity: Státní tiskárna cenin, s.p. (STC — Czech State Printing Works of Securities)
signals.signal: STC published an EU preliminary market consultation (PTK) for BIOMETRIC ENROLMENT KIOSKS — 'supply and operation of biometric enrolment kiosks' for a PLANNED above-threshold public contract. Estimated value CZK 50,000,000 excl. VAT. Main CPV 30233310 (fingerprint readers) plus 30231300 display units, 48900000 software packages, 72514000 computer facilities management, 48810000 information systems. Consultation questions cover technical feasibility, service and maintenance scope, per-component pricing, periodic inspections, FRAUD DETECTION AND PREVENTION capability, and delivery timelines. Responses were due 08/05/2026. As of 01/08/2026 the follow-on above-threshold tender had NOT yet been published on TED or NEN (NEN N006/26/P00000099 still shows status 'Not terminated'). Docs hosted on a second Czech E-ZAK instance, mfcr.ezak.cz.
signals.source_name: TED notice 291826-2026 (OJ S 82/2026), cross-checked against NEN N006/26/P00000099
signals.implies: The closest thing in Czechia to a Printec-shaped self-service opportunity. A biometric enrolment kiosk is functionally Printec's digital onboarding / eKYC stack in a hardened unattended enclosure: document scan, live fingerprint/face capture, liveness and fraud detection, back-office identity system, plus multi-year field service. Maps to Printec digital onboarding/eKYC, self-service kiosk hardware+integration and managed services. STC also issues Czech ID cards, passports and driving licences, so a win is a reference for identity-linked bank onboarding across the region.
signals.likelihood: Above-threshold tender highly likely to be published H2-2026/H1-2027 given PTK closed 08/05/2026 and a firm CZK 50m budget line
signals.followup: Watch NEN N006/26/P00000099 and the STC profile for the contract notice; request the PTK document from mfcr.ezak.cz/document_download_44166.html; contact Mgr. Petra Nádvorníková (nadvornikova.petra@stc.cz, +420 236031490) and Veronika Lacová (Lacova.Veronika@stc.cz) before the notice drops.

signals.entity: Česká pošta, s.p. (Czech Post) / Albacon Systems, a.s.
signals.signal: Czech Post runs a rolling stream of cash-equipment purchases and Albacon Systems, a.s. is the dominant incumbent. Awards published on TED: coin-rolling/packaging machines (CPV 30123630) CZK 296,406 on 29/07/2026 (TED 524698-2026), CZK 768,572 on 05/05/2026 (TED 305254-2026), CZK 920,268 on 30/01/2026 (TED 69695-2026), CZK 385,228 on 24/07/2025, CZK 233,532 on 02/05/2025, CZK 346,306 on 24/01/2025; banknote counters (CPV 30132200) CZK 234,000 on 30/01/2026 (TED 69049-2026), CZK 487,600 on 24/07/2025, CZK 56,800 on 02/05/2025.
signals.source_name: TED notice 524698-2026 (latest in series); TED 305254-2026; TED 69695-2026; TED 69049-2026
signals.implies: Czech Post is the single largest publicly-tendered cash-handling buyer in Czechia and it buys in many small tranches rather than one big deal — a recurring-revenue annuity rather than a project. Maps to Printec cash automation (counters, sorters, packaging) and managed services. Albacon Systems must be displaced tranche-by-tranche or via a framework bid, not by one campaign.
signals.likelihood: Further tranches near-certain — the series has run at roughly quarterly cadence for 18+ months
signals.followup: Register on TENDER ARENA (Czech Post's contracting-authority profile — it is a JSF app and NOT readable without a supplier login) and set a TED alert on buyer 'Česká pošta' + CPV 30123630/30132200/30132000; profile Albacon Systems a.s. pricing.

signals.entity: Česká pošta, s.p. / QEX CZ, a.s. and Bankovní technika spol. s r.o.
signals.signal: Two further cash-equipment incumbents sit alongside Albacon at Czech Post. QEX CZ, a.s. won BANKNOTE SORTERS (CPV 30132000) worth CZK 6,600,000 — the largest single cash-equipment award in the series (TED 400047-2025, 20/06/2025) — plus coin sorters (CPV 30132300) CZK 455,707 (24/01/2025), CZK 58,350 (02/05/2025) and CZK 3,890 (24/07/2025). Bankovní technika spol. s r.o. won coin sorters/counters worth CZK 1,950,000 (TED 468595-2025, 17/07/2025). Separately QEX CZ, a.s. bid for the ČNB coin-processing contract in 2021 but was excluded for an incomplete/unacceptable tender.
signals.source_name: TED notice 400047-2025; TED 468595-2025; ČNB E-ZAK profile XML (VZ-795)
signals.implies: Maps the full Czech cash-automation competitor set: Albacon Systems (counters/packaging), QEX CZ (sorters), Bankovní technika (counters/sorters), with Giesecke+Devrient owning the central-bank tier. All are local resellers/integrators rather than manufacturers, so Printec can compete either as a direct principal or by displacing one of them as the channel. Maps to Printec cash automation and recyclers.
signals.likelihood: Banknote-sorter refresh at Czech Post recurs on a multi-year cycle; next window plausible 2027
signals.followup: Pull the QEX CZ a.s. and Bankovní technika s.r.o. company filings from justice.cz to establish which OEM lines they carry; check whether either already represents a Printec-competitive brand in Czechia.

signals.entity: Česká národní banka (Czech National Bank) / Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH
signals.signal: ČNB's banknote-processing estate is locked to Giesecke+Devrient. Contract VZ-542 'Dodávka třídicích systémů pro zpracování bankovek' — supply and installation of 8 sorting systems plus supporting technology for banknote processing, plus 1 sorting system for the State Printing Works (STC), plus building works and ongoing operational support — was awarded to Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH (DE) at CZK 384,741,983.35 excl. VAT (CZK 465,537,799.85 incl. VAT), contract signed 20/12/2018. The estate was sized for an expected 800,000 bundles of 1,000 banknotes per year. Operational-support spend is still running: CZK 8,783,102.20 excl. VAT in 2024 and CZK 6,941,443.40 excl. VAT in 2025. Cash Processing Solutions Limited (GB) bid and was EXCLUDED for an incomplete or unacceptable tender.
signals.source_name: ČNB contracting-authority profile, machine-readable XML export (profile 342165), object VZ-542, VVZ ref Z2018-005301
signals.implies: The Czech central bank's high-speed sorting tier is a G+D monoculture with an eight-year-old estate and a live service annuity of roughly CZK 7-9m/yr. Realistic Printec routes are (a) the eventual replacement round, likely 2027-2029 on a typical 10-year lifecycle, and (b) nothing sooner. Maps to Printec cash automation and managed services. Also confirms G+D as the regional central-bank incumbent alongside its positions at NBS Serbia and Banka Slovenije already on the record.
signals.likelihood: No replacement tender visible before 2027; treat as long-cycle account development
signals.followup: Track ČNB's annual procurement plan and the E-ZAK XML feed for any 'třídicí systém' contract modification or replacement notice; the same feed is the cheapest early-warning channel.

signals.entity: Česká národní banka / Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH (coin tier)
signals.signal: ČNB contract VZ-795 'Dodávka a servis technologií pro zpracování mincí' — supply and servicing of coin-processing technology comprising electromagnetic-inspection equipment, optical-inspection equipment, coin adjustment equipment and EBKV containers for bulk loose coin — was awarded to Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH at CZK 109,037,103.00 excl. VAT (CZK 131,934,895.00 incl. VAT), contract signed 13/01/2022 after a negotiated procedure with publication (VVZ Z2020-044973). QEX CZ, a.s. (IČO 47116871) also bid and was excluded. Servicing spend continues: CZK 2,531,780.93 excl. VAT in 2024 and CZK 4,209,984.40 excl. VAT in 2025.
signals.source_name: ČNB contracting-authority profile XML export (profile 342165), object VZ-795, VVZ ref Z2020-044973
signals.implies: Confirms G+D holds both the banknote AND coin tiers at ČNB, so there is no split-supplier wedge at the central bank. The only Czech coin-equipment openings are at Czech Post and municipal/ministerial level. Maps to Printec cash automation. Useful negative for account planning: do not model a near-term ČNB coin opportunity.
signals.likelihood: Service contract runs on; no new coin tender expected before ~2029
signals.followup: Confirm the contract's stated duration by pulling the signed smlouva from the ČNB E-ZAK contract page for VZ-795.

signals.entity: SEFIRA spol. s r.o. (IČO 62907760) — Czech HSM/eIDAS integrator
signals.signal: SEFIRA has won the two most significant Czech public-sector HSM contracts of 2026, both supplying Entrust nShield hardware security modules. (1) Česká národní banka, 'Upgrade HSM modulů Entrust' — replacement of ČNB's 2 existing HSM modules with a newer version including software, installation, implementation and configuration: CZK 10,496,110.00 excl. VAT (CZK 12,700,293.00 incl. VAT), open procedure, tender deadline 19/02/2026, contract signed 11/03/2026, VVZ Z2026-001731. (2) Generální finanční ředitelství (Czech tax administration), 'Generační obnova HSM zařízení' — 2x Entrust nShield 5c plus Remote Admin Ready Cards v2.0 and 2x perpetual OBELISK Connector for HSM nShield 5c licences, used to create qualified electronic seals under eIDAS Regulation (EU) 910/2014: CZK 1,353,600.00 excl. VAT (CZK 1,637,856.00 incl. VAT), contract 26/7700/0932 signed 22/06/2026, NEN N006/26/V00013243.
signals.source_name: NEN N006/26/V00013243 result page; ČNB E-ZAK profile XML (VZ-1242)
signals.implies: Czechia's HSM demand is real and recurring but it is eIDAS/qualified-seal driven rather than payment-HSM driven, and SEFIRA plus its OBELISK platform is the gatekeeper on Entrust kit. Maps directly to Printec HSM/security. Printec's payment-HSM proposition (Thales payShield class, PIN/key management for acquiring) is a DIFFERENT segment that is not being tendered publicly here — it sits inside the private commercial banks. Treat SEFIRA as either the competitor to displace or the channel partner to co-bid with.
signals.likelihood: Further Czech public-sector HSM refreshes near-certain (MPSV, ČÚZK, DIA and MO all ran HSM tenders in 2024-2026)
signals.followup: Assess SEFIRA as a potential Czech channel partner; separately test whether Printec's payment-HSM and key-management managed service has any Czech public-sector angle (Státní pokladna / SPCSS) or is purely a commercial-bank sale.

signals.entity: Česká národní banka — physical security / FestTech s.r.o.
signals.signal: ČNB contract VZ-1188 'Obnova systému elektronických trezorových zámků trezorových dveří' — renewal of the electronic vault-door lock system across ČNB buildings including a remote administration system, plus warranty, out-of-warranty and post-warranty repairs and scheduled preventive maintenance. VAT); CZK 2,137,490.00 excl. VAT was drawn in 2025. VVZ ref Z2025-036180.
signals.source_name: ČNB contracting-authority profile XML export (profile 342165), object VZ-1188

Maps to Printec HSM/security in its physical-security sense and to managed services. Low direct fit for Printec's core but useful as an account-entry wedge and for understanding how ČNB slices its security spend.

signals.entity: Česká národní banka — OPEN TENDER, cash-centre handling equipment
signals.signal: OPEN above-threshold open procedure: ČNB 'Servis a opravy manipulační techniky' (servicing and repair of materials-handling equipment), divided into 5 lots by site — Lot A Praha (Senovážná 3), Lot B Hradec Králové (Hořická 1652), Lot C Brno, Lot D České Budějovice, Lot E Ostrava. These are ČNB's regional cash-processing and vault sites. CPV 42410000-3 (lifting and handling equipment) and 50000000-5 (repair and maintenance services). Published on profile 24/07/2026 approx.; DEADLINE FOR TENDERS 24/08/2026 10:00. System number P26V00000062, database ID 1304, VVZ registration Z2026-039840. Estimated value not published on the profile.
signals.implies: Peripheral to Printec's core (this is forklifts and pallet trucks inside cash centres, not cash-processing machinery) but it maps the exact five ČNB cash-centre locations that any future cash-automation or managed-services bid must cover, and it confirms ČNB's willingness to award per-site lots — a structure Printec could exploit in a services bid. Maps loosely to Printec managed services.
signals.followup: Do not bid; use the tender documents to harvest the ČNB cash-centre site list and service-level expectations for future proposals.

signals.entity: Ministerstvo vnitra ČR (Czech Ministry of the Interior) / Česká spořitelna, a.s.
signals.signal: The Ministry of the Interior operates a running framework for 'Bankovnictví — poskytování elektronického bankovnictví' (banking services / electronic banking via payment terminals), CPV 66110000 banking services + 30233300 smart card readers + 30144400 automatic fare-collection equipment. The framework was set at CZK 48,000,000 (TED 76079-2025, 04/02/2025) and Česká spořitelna, a.s. (Erste Group) has taken every call-off since: CZK 900,638.30 on 07/10/2025 (TED 654422-2025), CZK 1,194,646.35 on 20/01/2026 (TED 39366-2026), CZK 742,993.51 on 09/04/2026 (TED 240480-2026) and CZK 811,511.64 on 15/07/2026 (TED 489903-2026).
signals.implies: Czech public-sector card acceptance is bought as a BANK service, not as a terminal-vendor service — the acquirer (Česká spořitelna) bundles the terminals. That means Printec's POS/acquiring route into Czechia is via the acquirer, not via the public buyer: sell terminals, terminal management and managed services TO Česká spořitelna / ČSOB / KB rather than bidding public tenders. Maps to Printec POS/acquiring and managed services.
signals.likelihood: Framework call-offs continue quarterly; framework renewal likely 2028-2029
signals.followup: Reframe the Czech POS approach as an acquirer-channel sale; identify which terminal estate Česká spořitelna deploys on this framework and who supplies it.

signals.entity: Inspekce silniční dopravy (Czech Road Transport Inspectorate)
signals.signal: Small-scale open call 'Poskytování elektronického bankovnictví prostřednictvím platebních terminálů' — supply of MOBILE EMV chip payment terminals with full NFC/contactless support accepting VISA, Mastercard and Maestro, plus the associated acquiring, technical support and data management, for collecting fines and deposits roadside. Detailed requirements include: ruggedised case, operation from -10C to +40C, GPRS data SIM with border roaming or Wi-Fi, integrated receipt printer, 230V and vehicle USB-C charging, D+2 GROSS SETTLEMENT (transactions credited in full with fees invoiced separately), immutable variable-symbol identifier end to end, operator selection from at least 100 destination accounts shown on the display, manual entry of a >=10-character alphanumeric identifier, meal-voucher-card blocking, and daily PDF/CSV plus monthly transaction reporting. NEN N006/26/V00011619, published on profile 23/04/2026, deadline 15/05/2026, status still 'Not terminated' as of 01/08/2026.
signals.source_name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj, procurement detail N006/26/V00011619
signals.implies: A rare fully-specified Czech public POS requirement, and the spec is an almost exact template for a Printec mobile-acquiring/managed-POS proposition: rugged mPOS hardware, multi-account routing, reconciliation-grade reporting and gross settlement. Small in value but a usable reference account and a proof that Czech state bodies will buy terminals as a service. Maps to Printec POS/acquiring, transaction monitoring and managed services.
signals.likelihood: Award or cancellation imminent — evaluation has been open since May 2026
signals.followup: Check NEN for the result/winner; if cancelled, expect a re-run — contact Mgr. Veronika Zichová (veronika.zichova@insid.gov.cz) and pitch against the published spec.

signals.signal: Small-scale open call 'Poskytování bezpečnostních služeb chráněné pozemní přepravy hotovosti a cenin' — protected ground transport of cash and valuables with protection against theft, loss, damage or destruction, and HANDOVER TO AUTHORISED EMPLOYEES OF THE CZECH NATIONAL BANK IN PRAGUE, on a regular weekly schedule plus ad-hoc runs. Estimated value CZK 700,000 excl. VAT. CPV 60000000 transport services, with items 79710000 security services and 60100000 road transport. NEN N006/25/V00036604, published on profile 29/10/2025, tender deadline 13/11/2025, selection notice published 21/11/2025, status still shown as 'Not terminated' as of 01/08/2026. A predecessor contract ran from 2021 (N006/21/V00025898).
signals.source_name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj, procurement detail N006/25/V00036604
signals.implies: Confirms that Czech CIT (cash-in-transit) to the central bank is tendered publicly by state cultural/heritage bodies at modest values, and that Prague Castle still depends on manual cash collection. The commercial angle for Printec is not the CIT run itself but the alternative: cash recyclers / smart safes at the point of collection to cut CIT frequency. Maps to Printec cash automation and recyclers.
signals.likelihood: Contract likely already awarded; the NEN status field is stale
signals.followup: Retrieve the 'Oznámení o výběru' document from the NEN detail page to name the CIT winner; this identifies the active Czech CIT operators for partnership or displacement.

signals.entity: Czech commercial banking sector (ČSOB, Komerční banka, Česká spořitelna, Moneta, Air Bank) — STRUCTURAL FINDING
signals.signal: Exhaustive keyword sweeps of NEN (nen.nipez.cz), the whole national e-procurement portal covering all Czech contracting authorities, returned ZERO results for 'bankomat' (ATM) and ZERO for 'POS terminál'. Cash-related hits are confined to counting machines ('počítačka bankovek', 10 hits, all ministries/police/hospitals), coin counters, safes and CIT. Czech Post's own NEN profile carries only two tenders (both laptop purchases); its real procurement runs on the TENDER ARENA platform. Czech retail banks are private companies outside Act No. 134/2016 Coll. and publish nothing. Correspondingly, TED shows no ATM or self-service-banking notice from any Czech buyer in 2025-2026.
signals.source_name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj, public contracts search (keyword filters via the p:vz:nazev path parameter)
signals.implies: Decisive for Printec's Czech go-to-market: there is NO tender-driven route into the Czech ATM, recycler or POS market. Czechia must be worked as a direct commercial/enterprise sale to the banks and to Česká pošta's commercial buying function, plus the two genuine public openings identified this run (STC biometric kiosks, and the recurring Czech Post cash-equipment tranches). Reallocating tender-monitoring effort in Czechia toward direct account coverage is the actionable conclusion.
signals.likelihood: Structural and stable — will not change absent a change in Czech public-procurement law
signals.followup: Stop treating Czechia as a tender market for ATM/POS. Stand up direct coverage of ČSOB, KB, Česká spořitelna, Moneta and Air Bank, and register on TENDER ARENA for Česká pošta.

signals.entity: Česká pošta, s.p. / PHOBOS, spol. s r.o.

That is the operational pain that cash recyclers and smart safes at the counter address. Maps to Printec cash automation/recyclers as a displacement argument rather than a like-for-like bid.

The repeated reissues and the value cut from CZK 27m to CZK 23m suggest the city is struggling to get compliant bids — a classic opening for a vendor that can package hardware, EMV acceptance and managed service together. signals.signal: Small-scale tender 'Dodání hodnotové počítačky bankovek' (supply of a value-counting banknote counter — a machine that counts and totals banknotes by denomination rather than merely by piece), NEN N006/25/V00035849, tender deadline 31/10/2025, status still shown as 'Neukončen' (not terminated) as of 01/08/2026. coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed). Three distinct primary entry points, all opened directly. (1) CNB E-ZAK (ezak.cnb.cz): the profile HTML is GET-readable, and I found a far better route than page-scraping — the ISVZ machine-readable export at https://ezak.cnb.cz/XMLdataVZ?od=DDMMYYYY&do=DDMMYYYY, which returned all 276 CNB procurement objects with full award data (winner name, ICO, contract price incl./excl. VAT, contract date, per-year drawdown, excluded bidders and reasons). This is how the Giesecke+Devrient, SEFIRA, FestTech and Cash Processing Solutions facts were established from source rather than from press. Constraint: the feed rejects ranges over 366 days and any range spanning 01/07/2024, so it must be pulled in windows. (2) NEN (nen.nipez.cz): the standard GET query-string parameters (?nazev=, ?zadavatelNazev=) are SILENTLY IGNORED and return the unfiltered default list — a trap that produces false positives. The working syntax is the path segment /verejne-zakazky/p:vz:nazev=<urlencoded> and /verejne-zakazky/p:vz:zadavatelNazev=<urlencoded>, which does filter server-side; detail and result pages are readable at /en/verejne-zakazky/detail-zakazky/<code> and .../vysledek. Ran 24 Czech and English keyword sweeps (bankomat, samoobsluzny, tridic/tridicka, hotovost, penezni, platebni karty, platebni terminal, POS terminal, ostraha, preprava cenin, trezor, pocitacka, bankovek, minci, kiosk, vkladovy, HSM, AML, identifikace klienta, Czech POINT, bankovni sluzby) plus issuer sweeps on Ceska posta and Statni tiskarna cenin. (3) TED API v3 (api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search, POST): worked without authentication; ran a broad Czech in-scope CPV query (169 notices) and a focused cash-handling CPV query (86 notices, 2025-2026) plus buyer-scoped queries on Ceska posta (294 notices), CNB (377) and STC (66). TED notice PDFs were downloaded and extracted locally with pdfminer.six per the playbook (the WebFetch summariser lost the value and deadline fields on the STC notice; local extraction recovered them). Deliberate variation vs the previous run: this run used the ISVZ profile-XML channel and the TED REST API rather than notice-by-notice HTML reading, which is why award values, excluded bidders and per-year contract drawdowns are present. GENUINE GAPS, honestly stated: (a) Ceska posta's real contracting-authority profile is on TENDER ARENA (tenderarena.cz), a JSF single-page application that returns a 1.5KB script shell to any unauthenticated fetch — I could not enumerate its live tenders, so Czech Post coverage here rests entirely on the TED notices it is obliged to publish, which covers above-threshold and framework call-offs but NOT its below-threshold buying; (b) Czech commercial banks publish nothing and this is reported as a structural finding rather than a gap; (c) the STC above-threshold biometric-kiosk tender itself does not yet exist to be read — only the market consultation does; (d) I did not resolve the winner of the Prague Castle CIT contract because the selection notice is a document download rather than a data field.

Confirms the playbook rule: extract TED PDFs locally, do not trust the fetch-tool summary.
